purpose: The interaction layer as designed and as built: the verb spine, the target grammar, the skill rhythm, the gate object, the next-action ladder, the voice law, and the vocabulary settlement. Its counterpart to datamodel.json's 'ideal model' is not another JSON file — the ideal is prose, in methodology/README.md and AGENTS.md, because a fourth restatement of the theory is the disease this layer treats. What this file adds is the measurement: every surface records what it expresses (a pointer into the theory) or what it contradicts, and every claim carries a file:line and the quote that must still be there.

authority.note: Skills and agent prompts reference the shared core; they do not restate it. Prohibitions are restated wherever they bind, byte-identical; explanations are stated once.

driftTest: tests/test_design_pointers.py — every {file, line, quote} in design/*.json must still resolve. A quote that moved lines warns; a quote that vanished fails.

spine.owns: getting material in, generated or written; the adapter is the learning exercise
spine.note: The only verb that creates targets rather than consuming them, so it accepts a source expression as well.

spine.owns: authoring and repairing the substrate; the single writer
where a register stands, and triage when an apply bounced
spine.note: Generalized from post-apply triage. Its mechanical half is `./ch author --status`, which is deterministic; the skill judges only what is left genuinely ambiguous. Before this it was referenced from exactly one line in the repo.

expresses.quote: The learner works the substrate two ways

spine.note: The missing reading. Production built the substrate; nothing used it. The coach lives in Claude Code because that is where instructions are actually typed — the skill the substrate exists to teach.

plugin.scope: project — shared with anyone working in this repo, not personal config
plugin.agentsLoadByConvention: plugin.json declares skills but NOT agents: an explicit "agents" array validates and then loads nothing. The agents/ directory is picked up on its own, which is how beads does it.
plugin.pathIsPortable: The marketplace path is ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, so the committed file carries no machine-specific path. `claude plugin marketplace list` reads the user registry rather than project settings, so that expansion could not be confirmed from the CLI; if it fails on a fresh clone, `claude plugin marketplace add ./ --scope project` rewrites it.

cli.equivalence: ./ch <cmd> == uv run python -m tools.lingua <cmd>; both run from the repo root
cli.rationale: A hint nobody can paste is not a hint. `uv run python -m tools.lingua author --apply` is 43 characters of ceremony in every printed next-action.

forms.means: a corpus, when it has exactly one register
a chapter, when one mounted register matches
a chapter, when the corpus has one register

grammar.wasBefore: Three resolvers with three acceptance sets — a chapter-only resolver, an author-target resolver, and a work-dir resolver that alone accepted a bare corpus name. The skills documented three grammars and one was narrower than its own tooling.

rules: Orient: run ./ch where before beginning work.
Target: resolve and echo the expansion before acting.
Gates: the only beat permitted to ask the user a question.
Report: state line, then a table whose first column is the full chapter id, then exactly one next action.

modeledOn.quote: Each dimension document follows a fixed skeleton

gate.law: A gate that cannot show its material is a bug, not a gate.

instances.absorbs: name variant, origin-already-mounted, name collision, pull-before-register — four separate offers before
which generator, with what options, producing how many chapters, and is its output reproducible — one gate over the staged result rather than four questions before it exists
instances.materialIsTheOutput: The census and the recipe are proposals; what the gate shows is a staged page in full plus the real chapter count, computed by the same adapter the register will run.

instances.note: The dimension choice moved here from the intake form. It is the one irreversible decision in the system and it used to be asked before the source had been explored. Moving it also dissolved a live bug: the re-mount path skipped the form, then referenced a form answer that on that path did not exist.

materialFrom.quote: A gate that cannot show its material is a bug

instances.note: Both definitions are now printed with their anchors, and both branches are runnable commands. The reject branch is demote_conflicts applied mechanically to a second payload file, which let /ch:translate delete its 'editing a payload file is allowed' exception entirely.

ladder.note: Rung 7 is the design in one string: when production is done, the next thing is study. The ladder used to simply end.

voice.rule: Every next-step hint is copy-pasteable in full.
Human-facing lines print the full chapter id; local ids and work-dir keys are file forms.
Exit 0 always states what is now true; silence is never success.
Every state token printed has a legend.
One next action, and it agrees with the skills.
Case carries severity: REJECTED/FAILED/HELD block progress.
Non-zero-exit problems to stderr; recorded-for-later problems to stdout.

Ratified the concept, retired the word — in prose and new code. The web/ rename and the chroma collection rename are deferred: both touch persisted state.

vocabulary.note: The directory was corpora/ until the environment grew a second room. A corpus is what you read; a workspace repo is what you write. One flat directory could not say which relationship a checkout had, so the layout became declared config (chiron.yaml) resolved in one place (tools/lingua/devenv.py) and readable with `./ch devenv`.
The only room discovery scans. Anything else under the root is a stray, named by `./ch devenv` and `./ch check` rather than silently half-mounted.

vocabulary.concept: the room prompts are applied in
vocabulary.note: Scaffold only: a directory, a config key, validation and a read-only CLI surface. No verb mounts into it or edits it yet.

reads: v<N>/chroma/ (a ranking accelerator, never a dependency)
study.closesTheLoop: A word the lexicon lacks is reported as a substrate gap with a runnable /ch:translate — study failure becomes a production action.

gaps: The state line is not in the manifest, so web/ cannot print the byte-identical string. Putting it there means manifest v6 → v7 across tools/lingua/manifest.py, web/lib/content.ts, tests, README and AGENTS.md. Deferred deliberately: this pass changes no machine contract.

`bit` survives in web/ (navigator-types.ts, /api/bit, CommandPalette) and as the chroma collection name and .bits-fingerprint. Renaming the collection needs a paired fingerprint rename or every existing store breaks.

The PreToolUse guard that would make the devenv/ invariants enforced rather than restated is not wired; .claude/settings.json still has an empty hooks block. The SessionStart hook ships in the plugin manifest instead.
Noun-phrase extraction in grade() is n-gram longest-match over surface forms plus a stopword filter. It is deliberately coverage, not grammar, and will be imperfect on long instructions.

design/datamodel.json and design/ui-map.json carry `source` pointers without `quote`, so the drift test can only check that their files and line ranges still exist. Backfilling quotes would make them content-checkable too.

`claude plugin marketplace update` does not re-copy a directory-source plugin while its manifest version is unchanged, so an edit under plugins/ch/ needs an uninstall+install to take effect. Bumping the version on every skill edit is the alternative.

Generation provenance is not in the manifest, so the viewer cannot show that a chapter was generated or by what. Putting it there means manifest v6 → v7 across tools/lingua/manifest.py, web/lib/content.ts and the tests; deliberately deferred, since there is no viewer surface for it yet.

generatedMaterial.why: An undocumented repo has a working language but no prose to anchor it to. A documentation generator emits the missing half: the identifiers, and the authors' own doc comments describing them.
generatedMaterial.shape: Generation is a mount-time preprocessor. It writes a Markdown tree beside source/; from the adapter down nothing knows the material was generated.
generatedMaterial.belongsTo: /ch:mount — generating material is getting material in

subcommands.does: what a generator would find here, and the closed tool registry
keep it, git-committed, with its recipe

selection.behindTheScenes: /ch:mount spawns it without asking; the user meets the choice at GATE M with the output in front of them.
selection.proposesData: It writes a recipe, never a command. The tool registry is closed, so nothing free-form reaches a shell.
selection.mayDecline: A corpus that should not be generated is a correct answer, and the cheapest one.

determinism.law: Anchors are pinned to a chapter's content_hash, which is computed over generated bytes. A generator that varies would mark a whole register stale on every regeneration.

enforcedBy.quote: generate -> normalize -> generate again -> compare -> promote

generatedMaterial.gapItCloses: codetree could always chapter an undocumented repo, but the authoring agents then anchored to raw source.
generatedMaterial.gapItOpens: A derived tree behind its source reads ok, because content_hash only knows the generated bytes. `./ch doc --status` is the only thing that sees it, and /ch:verify reports it as its own line.

expresses.quote: prose is what chiron wants from an undocumented repo

chapteredBy.quote: tree always yields the same chapters
